description: MAP screen of number-game variants (2026-10-31, exp3 iter_3/cand_3) — separate kappa for "contains digit" rules gains ~20 nats; pooling them with final-digit salience loses ~60
metadata:

name: decision-rule-map-screen
description: MAP screen of decision rules on top of the incumbent number-game learner (experiment3 iter_3) — which response rules the data support
metadata:
  type: project
---
2026-10-31, experiment3 iter_3/candidate_2 (decision-rule brief). The incumbent gamma_shaped_range_width_prior with a swapped response stage was screened by MAP (find_MAP + observedlogp, ~2 min each, in parallel; script /tmp/drule/run.py):
base -2556.6; log-odds yes-bias -> bias 0.04 (null); lapse+guess -> lapse 7e-7 (null); odds power d -> 0.895, -2554.4 (+2.2); OR-of-2 sampled concepts -2659; majority-of-3 -2635; AND-of-2 -2785.
**Why:** bias and lapse fit to the null, so the novelty gate would reject them (see [[interval-prefix-sum-speedup]] gotcha); sampling-based rules lose badly.
**How to apply:** submitted conservative_belief_reporting (odds^d, d ~ Beta(3,1), so it can only compress). Don't re-spend slots on lapse or bias for this learner. MAP-screen a nested param before committing.
---
name: interval-prefix-sum-speedup
description: How to make number-game interval-concept models fast enough for the 30-min admission fit (prefix-sum regions instead of 1.5M sparse scatters)
metadata:
  type: project
---
The live number-game models enumerate every (set, interval) pair (~524k) and every (cell, interval) hit (~1.5M scatter), costing ~55-115 ms per gradient; several candidates (2026-10-31, experiment3 iter_1) were rejected "too slow to fit".
Fix used in pedagogical_teacher_sampling (iter_1/candidate_0_repair_1): an interval weight factors as G_k(a,b) (set-independent: width prior x W(a,b)^(-beta k), k = examples inside, 0..4) times a constant per region (intervals holding the same examples form a rectangle in (a,b)). Take 2D prefix sums of G_k and read rectangle sums by 4 corner gathers (~1.8k regions, ~7.5k target-clipped rectangles). Subtract per-k max of log G before exp. Gradient fell 114 -> 22 ms, p_yes identical to 1e-13; warm-start NUTS sampled 1000 iters/2 chains in 244 s.
**Why:** a second too-slow rejection is final for a slot.
**How to apply:** reuse for any candidate built on the interval machinery; also dedupe exception-neighbourhood member tables (pm.Data matrix @ weights) rather than per-concept gathers.
Ready-made fast template of the incumbent (anchored side channel + prefix sums): experiment3/model_loop/models/set_size_discounted_evidence.py — set zeta to 0 / delete it to get the incumbent. Used for iter_2/candidate_0 (parity_markedness_odd_cost): the smoke check took ~4.5 min total and 86 s of sampling.

Port to incumbent anchored_neighbourhood_side_channel (iter_2/candidate_2, even_leaning_rule_prior): use x weights exp(-gamma log x), reg_log_x = sum log x of held examples, drop the pedagogical LOG_D centring; matches the incumbent's p_yes to 5e-13, gradient ~14 ms. Copy that file as the fast base for any incumbent refinement.
Equivalence-check gotcha: model.compile_fn(...)(ip) with a hand-edited initial_point silently assigned values to the wrong params; use pytensor.function(model.value_vars, *model.replace_rvs_by_values([p_yes])) with positional args.
Reused 2026-10-31 (experiment3 iter_2/candidate_1, even_favouring_rule_prior): the prefix-sum port of anchored_neighbourhood_side_channel (tw = x^-gamma, reg_log_x = sum log x) matches the incumbent to 1.5e-11 at 9 ms/grad vs 51 ms. Equivalence-check script: iter_2/candidate_1/scratch/eq.py.
Pitfall: `model.compile_fn(model["p_yes"])` SAMPLES the RVs (non-deterministic output); wrap with `model.replace_rvs_by_values([...])[0]` before comparing models.
Weak-sampling variant (iter_2/candidate_1 retry, weak_sampling_doubt): the k=0 prefix table is the width prior alone, so a weak-sampling term per region is just rect(corner - k*101*101) * const — no new tables. Note: an earlier session of this same slot left no files (lost); peers in iter_2 already took the even-bias critique (candidates 0, 2, 5), so avoid duplicating it.
Reused again (iter_2/candidate_3, gamma_shaped_range_width_prior): derived from iter_2/candidate_2/candidate.py by dropping zeta; check_candidate passed in 3.4 min (~55-78 s sampling). Note iter_2 candidates 0,1,2,5 all targeted the even-bias critique, so pick other critique stats for diversity.
Reused (iter_2/candidate_4, weber_scaled_exception_neighbourhood): candidate_2 base minus zeta, radius prior made centre-dependent via a (100, radii) extent table from a cumsum of (n/50)^-nu, gathered by new cls_x; H_MAX 6. Check passed in 4.5 min (94 s sampling).
Novelty gate lesson (2026-10-31, iter_2/candidate_4): the Weber-scaled radius prior (nested, extra param nu -> 0) was REJECTED as near-duplicate of the incumbent (RMSE 0.0019 < 0.002). Nested refinements whose new param can fit to the null get rejected; prefer a structural change with no off-switch. Repair (candidate_4_repair_1, range_plus_exception_side_channel): range-plus-neighbourhood side-channel concepts as region rectangles clipped clear of the neighbourhood (rx_* arrays, ~6.7k rects, 34k target-clipped), sharing alpha/rho/omega; RMSE vs incumbent 0.066, 27 ms/grad.
Iter_3/candidate_5 (gamma_width_range_plus_exception): grafted the incumbent's gamma width prior (mean_width, width_shape) onto models/range_plus_exception_side_channel.py — only 2 lines change (sigma -> mean_width/width_shape, log_width formula). Combines the two best single refinements of anchored_neighbourhood_side_channel.
Reused (iter_3/candidate_0, pattern_violation_anchored_exception, order-effect brief): copied models/gamma_shaped_range_width_prior.py (the rank-0 incumbent itself is already the fast prefix-sum form) and restricted exception anchors to missed examples preceded by a rule-covered example, has_off -> pm.Data rule_anchorable. Structural (no off-switch) to dodge the novelty gate. Check OK, ~31 s sampling per smoke run.
Composition (iter_3/candidate_4, gamma_width_range_plus_exception): range_plus_exception_side_channel.py with its sigma Erlang line swapped for the incumbent's gamma width prior (mean_width, width_shape) — a 2-line edit; check passed in 3.6 min (70 s sampling).
Similarity-slot data point (iter_3/candidate_1, nearest_example_radius_concepts): replacing ranges entirely with "within r of an example" neighbourhood unions (r 0..99, (sets*100,100) mask @ x^-gamma) passes check in 3.3 min, but the smoke-fit log-lik was -2967 vs the incumbent's ELPD of about -2623. Ranges (filling in the gap between examples) look essential; don't drop them.
Duplicate-slot lesson (2026-10-31, iter_3/candidate_5): two slots in the same round independently built gamma_width_range_plus_exception; the second was rejected (RMSE 0). Before composing two top refinements, check models/ for a same-round twin. Repair (candidate_5_repair_1, pedagogical_teacher_gamma_width): pedagogical_teacher_sampling.py with sigma swapped for the gamma width prior (same 2-line edit); check OK, 123 s sampling, smoke log-lik -2566.8.

---
name: participant-segmentation
description: exp3 responses.csv has no participant_id but rows are ordered; trial_index==0 resets mark 15 participants x 450 trials
metadata:
  type: project
---
In experiment3 `responses.csv`, participants can be recovered with `(trial_index==0).cumsum()`: 15 participants, 450 trials each. Each (set, target) cell has 5 responses. Raw yes-rates come in blocks of 5 (~0.23, ~0.37, ~0.30), so participants seem to share stimulus lists in groups of 5.

**Why:** this makes participant-level PPC statistics possible (breadth dispersion, lag-1 residual dependence) even though there is no id column.
**How to apply:** compute residuals against the cell mean before comparing participants, so differences between stimulus lists don't get counted as individual differences. Related: [[decision-rule-map-screen]].

"""Salient contained-digit rules.

Refinement of `gamma_shaped_range_width_prior`: the same 45 rules
(final-digit rules boosted by kappa), compressed-number-line sampling of range
members with a gamma-shaped width prior (fitted shape and mean), tempered size
principle (beta), exception rate eps, and "rule plus an example-anchored
neighbourhood" concepts emitted through a side channel (rate omega). The one
change: rules about a digit a numeral contains ("contains digit d") are read
off the written numerals and are perceptually salient, so they get their own
fitted prior boost kappa_c. When every example contains a common digit in
different places, people extend it to distant numbers containing that digit
(e.g. numbers in that digit's decade) more than the incumbent predicts.

Intervals are not enumerated per set: an interval's weight factors into a
set-independent table over (a, b) for each count of examples inside times a
constant per region of intervals holding the same examples, so region sums
(and those holding a target) come from 2D prefix sums.
"""


import numpy as np
import pymc as pm
import pytensor.tensor as pt

NUMBERS = np.arange(1, 101)


def rule_concepts():
    rules = {
        "odd": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 2 == 1],
        "primes": [n for n in NUMBERS if n > 1 and all(n % a for a in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1))],
        "squares": [n * n for n in range(1, 11)],
        "cubes": [n**3 for n in range(1, 5)],
        "powers of 2, not 32": [2, 4, 8, 16, 64],
        "powers of 2, or 37": [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 37, 64],
        "even": list(range(2, 101, 2)),
    }
    rules.update({f"multiples of {m}": list(range(m, 101, m)) for m in [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12]})
    rules.update({f"powers of {m}": [m**k for k in range(1, 8) if m**k <= 100] for m in range(2, 11)})
    rules.update({f"ends in {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 10 == d] for d in range(10)})
    rules.update({f"contains digit {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if str(d) in str(n)] for d in range(10)})
    return rules


RULE_NAMES = list(rule_concepts().keys())
RULES = list(rule_concepts().values())
RULE_CONTAINS = np.array([n.startswith("contains") for n in RULE_NAMES], dtype="float64")
RULE_SALIENT = np.array([n in ("odd", "even") or n.startswith("ends in") for n in RULE_NAMES], dtype="float64")
N_RULES = len(RULES)
RULE_MEMBERSHIP = np.array([np.isin(NUMBERS, c) for c in RULES], dtype="float64")
RULE_SIZE = RULE_MEMBERSHIP.sum(axis=1)
LOG_NUMBERS = np.log(NUMBERS.astype("float64"))
GRID_A, GRID_B = np.meshgrid(NUMBERS, NUMBERS, indexing="ij")
TRI = (GRID_B >= GRID_A).astype("float64")
GRID_W = np.clip(GRID_B - GRID_A, 0, 99)  # width - 1
K_RANGE = np.arange(5, dtype="float64")
MAX_EX = 4
H_MAX = 3
H_RADII = np.arange(H_MAX + 1, dtype="float64")
SIZES = np.arange(1, 101, dtype="float64")
LOG_SIZE_COUNT = np.log(101 - SIZES)


def _scatter_sum(n, index, values):
    return pt.inc_subtensor(pt.zeros(n)[index], values)


with pm.Model() as model:
    rule_k = pm.Data("rule_k", np.zeros((1, N_RULES)))
    set_n = pm.Data("set_n", np.ones(1))
    reg_set = pm.Data("reg_set", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    reg_k = pm.Data("reg_k", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))  # examples inside the region's intervals
    reg_log_x = pm.Data("reg_log_x", np.zeros(1))  # sum of log x over them
    reg_corner = pm.Data("reg_corner", np.zeros((1, 4), dtype="int64"))
    hit_cell = pm.Data("hit_cell", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    hit_reg = pm.Data("hit_reg", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    hit_corner = pm.Data("hit_corner", np.zeros((1, 4), dtype="int64"))
    cell_set = pm.Data("cell_set", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    cell_rule_member = pm.Data("cell_rule_member", np.zeros((1, N_RULES)))
    row_cell = pm.Data("row_cell", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    cls_set = pm.Data("cls_set", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    cls_rule = pm.Data("cls_rule", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    cls_h = pm.Data("cls_h", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    cls_extra_n = pm.Data("cls_extra_n", np.ones(1))
    cls_e = pm.Data("cls_e", np.zeros(1))
    cls_m = pm.Data("cls_m", np.ones(1))
    chit_cell = pm.Data("chit_cell", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    chit_cls = pm.Data("chit_cls", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    rating = pm.Data("rating", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))

    lambda_0 = pm.Beta("lambda_0", 2, 2)
    beta = pm.LogNormal("beta", mu=0.0, sigma=0.5)
    eps = pm.Beta("eps", 2, 5)
    gamma = pm.HalfNormal("gamma", sigma=1.0)
    mean_width = pm.LogNormal("mean_width", mu=np.log(40.0), sigma=1.0)  # typical range width
    width_shape = pm.LogNormal("width_shape", mu=np.log(2.0), sigma=0.75)  # gamma shape of the width prior (2 = Erlang)
    kappa = pm.Normal("kappa", mu=0.0, sigma=1.5)
    kappa_c = pm.Normal("kappa_c", mu=0.0, sigma=1.5)
    alpha = pm.Beta("alpha", 1, 4)
    rho = pm.LogNormal("rho", mu=0.0, sigma=1.0)
    omega = pm.Beta("omega", 2, 6)

    n_sets = set_n.shape[0]
    n_cells = cell_set.shape[0]
    log_noise = pt.log(eps) - np.log(100)
    rule_in = pt.log((1 - eps) / RULE_SIZE + eps / 100)
    rule_log_lik = rule_k * rule_in[None, :] + (set_n[:, None] - rule_k) * log_noise
    rule_score = kappa * RULE_SALIENT + kappa_c * RULE_CONTAINS
    log_rule_prior = rule_score - pm.math.logsumexp(rule_score)
    has_off = pt.gt(set_n[:, None] - rule_k, 0.5)
    log_rules = pt.log(lambda_0) + pt.log1p(-alpha * has_off) + log_rule_prior[None, :] + beta * rule_log_lik
    shift = pt.max(log_rules, axis=1)
    w_rules = pt.exp(log_rules - shift[:, None])

    # Rule plus anchored neighbourhood, two channels (rule w.p. 1 - omega, neighbourhood w.p. omega).
    log_h_prior = -rho * H_RADII - pm.math.logsumexp(-rho * H_RADII)
    side_rule_in = pt.log((1 - eps) * (1 - omega) / RULE_SIZE + eps / 100)
    cls_x_in = pt.log((1 - eps) * omega / cls_extra_n + eps / 100)
    k_rule = rule_k[cls_set, cls_rule]
    log_cls = (
        pt.log(lambda_0) + pt.log(alpha) + log_rule_prior[cls_rule] + log_h_prior[cls_h]
        - pt.log(cls_m)
        + beta * (
            k_rule * side_rule_in[cls_rule]
            + cls_e * cls_x_in
            + (set_n[cls_set] - k_rule - cls_e) * log_noise
        )
    )
    w_cls = pt.exp(log_cls - shift[cls_set])
    w_aug = _scatter_sum(n_sets * N_RULES, cls_set * N_RULES + cls_rule, w_cls).reshape((n_sets, N_RULES))

    # Intervals: members drawn with weight x^-gamma, P(x | [a, b]) = x^-gamma / W(a, b).
    # Weight of [a, b] = G_k(a, b) * C(set, region), G_k = P(width) W^(-beta k).
    cum_w = pt.concatenate([pt.zeros(1), pt.cumsum(pt.exp(-gamma * LOG_NUMBERS))])
    log_w_int = pt.log(pt.maximum(cum_w[GRID_B] - cum_w[GRID_A - 1], 1e-30))
    # Gamma width prior: log P(range of width s) = (width_shape - 1) log s - s width_shape / mean_width - log Z.
    log_width = (width_shape - 1) * pt.log(SIZES) - SIZES * width_shape / mean_width
    log_z = pm.math.logsumexp(LOG_SIZE_COUNT + log_width)
    log_size_prior = pt.log1p(-lambda_0) + log_width - log_z
    log_g = log_size_prior[GRID_W][None, :, :] - beta * K_RANGE[:, None, None] * log_w_int[None, :, :]
    log_g = pt.where(TRI[None] > 0, log_g, -1e4)
    g_max = pt.max(log_g, axis=(1, 2))
    g = pt.exp(log_g - g_max[:, None, None])
    prefix = pt.zeros((MAX_EX + 1, 101, 101))
    prefix = pt.set_subtensor(prefix[:, 1:, 1:], pt.cumsum(pt.cumsum(g, axis=1), axis=2)).reshape((-1,))

    def rect(corner):
        sums = prefix[corner[:, 0]] - prefix[corner[:, 1]] - prefix[corner[:, 2]] + prefix[corner[:, 3]]
        return pt.maximum(sums, 0.0)

    reg_const = pt.exp(
        g_max[reg_k]
        + beta * (reg_k * pt.log1p(-eps) - gamma * reg_log_x + (set_n[reg_set] - reg_k) * log_noise)
        - shift[reg_set]
    )
    w_reg = rect(reg_corner) * reg_const
    covered = _scatter_sum(n_cells, hit_cell, rect(hit_corner) * reg_const[hit_reg])

    z = w_rules.sum(axis=1) + w_aug.sum(axis=1) + _scatter_sum(n_sets, reg_set, w_reg)
    numer = (
        (w_rules[cell_set] * cell_rule_member).sum(axis=1)
        + (w_aug[cell_set] * cell_rule_member).sum(axis=1)
        + _scatter_sum(n_cells, chit_cell, w_cls[chit_cls])
        + covered
    )
    in_concept = numer / z[cell_set]

    p_yes = pm.Deterministic("p_yes", pt.clip(in_concept[row_cell], 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6))
    pm.Bernoulli("response", p=p_yes, observed=rating)


def prepare_observed(rows):
    """Rows carry `number_set` ("16,8", in presented order), `target` and `rating`."""
    sets = [tuple(int(x) for x in str(r["number_set"]).split(",")) for r in rows]
    unique = list(dict.fromkeys(sets))
    index = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(unique)}
    trial_cells = [(index[s], int(r["target"])) for s, r in zip(sets, rows)]
    cells = list(dict.fromkeys(trial_cells))
    cell_index = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(cells)}

    def corners(k, a0, a1, b0, b1):  # flat prefix indices for the sum over a0..a1 x b0..b1
        base = k * 101 * 101
        return [base + a1 * 101 + b1, base + (a0 - 1) * 101 + b1, base + a1 * 101 + b0 - 1, base + (a0 - 1) * 101 + b0 - 1]

    reg_rows, reg_corner, set_regs = [], [], []
    for i, st in enumerate(unique):
        e = [0] + sorted(set(st)) + [101]
        mine = []
        for gi in range(len(e) - 1):
            for gj in range(gi, len(e) - 1):
                a0, a1 = e[gi] + 1, min(e[gi + 1], 100)
                b0, b1 = max(e[gj], 1), e[gj + 1] - 1
                if a0 > a1 or b0 > b1:
                    continue
                held = [x for x in st if a1 <= x <= b0] if gj > gi else []
                mine.append((len(reg_rows), a0, a1, b0, b1, len(held)))
                reg_rows.append((i, len(held), float(sum(LOG_NUMBERS[x - 1] for x in held))))
                reg_corner.append(corners(len(held), a0, a1, b0, b1))
        set_regs.append(mine)
    hit_cell, hit_reg, hit_corner = [], [], []
    for c, (i, t) in enumerate(cells):
        for r, a0, a1, b0, b1, k in set_regs[i]:
            ca1, cb0 = min(a1, t), max(b0, t)
            if a0 <= ca1 and cb0 <= b1:
                hit_cell.append(c)
                hit_reg.append(r)
                hit_corner.append(corners(k, a0, ca1, cb0, b1))
    reg = np.array(reg_rows, dtype="float64")

    cls_rows, cls_extra, set_cls = [], [], []
    for i, st in enumerate(unique):
        ex_count = np.bincount(np.array(st), minlength=101)[1:]
        mine = []
        for r in range(N_RULES):
            in_rule = RULE_MEMBERSHIP[r] > 0
            centres = sorted({x for x in st if not in_rule[x - 1]})

                    cls_rows.append((i, r, h, len(extra), ex_count[extra - 1].sum(), len(centres)))
                    cls_extra.append(set(extra.tolist()))
        set_cls.append(mine)
    chit_cell, chit_cls = [], []
    for c, (i, t) in enumerate(cells):

                chit_cell.append(c)
                chit_cls.append(j)
    cls = np.array(cls_rows, dtype="float64")

    return {
        "rule_k": np.stack([RULE_MEMBERSHIP[:, np.array(s) - 1].sum(axis=1) for s in unique]),
        "set_n": np.array([float(len(s)) for s in unique]),
        "reg_set": reg[:, 0].astype("int64"),
        "reg_k": reg[:, 1].astype("int64"),

        "cell_rule_member": np.stack([RULE_MEMBERSHIP[:, t - 1] for _, t in cells]),
        "row_cell": np.array([cell_index[c] for c in trial_cells], dtype="int64"),

    sample_synthetic_responses, where the caller has rows but not a CSV file.

doc_end=src.index('"""',3)+3
doc='''"""Individual response criteria.

Refinement of `conservative_belief_reporting`: people infer the program's
concept as the best Bayesian learner does (here the current best,
`salient_contained_digit_rules`: 55 rules with final-digit rules boosted by
kappa and contained-digit rules by kappa_c, compressed-number-line ranges under

and rule-plus-anchored-neighbourhood concepts emitted through a side channel),
and the distortion lies only in how they turn that belief into a yes/no
report. The one change: instead of one shared conservative compression of the
belief odds, each person has their own response criterion, a stable lean
toward "yes" or toward "no" that shifts the log-odds of every answer they give
(criteria drawn from a population distribution whose spread is fitted). So
the same belief is endorsed more by some people than by others, consistently
across all their trials, and the population as a whole hedges toward
fifty-fifty only through this spread.

Participants are recovered from the restarts of `trial_index` at 0. For a
stimulus row with no participant, the prediction averages over the population
distribution of criteria (Gauss-Hermite quadrature).

set-independent table over (a, b) for each count of examples inside times a

(and those holding a target) come from 2D prefix sums.

s=s.replace('    row_cell = pm.Data("row_cell", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))\n','    row_cell = pm.Data("row_cell", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))\n    row_person = pm.Data("row_person", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))\n    row_known = pm.Data("row_known", np.zeros(1))  # 1 if the row belongs to a known participant\n')

s=s.replace('    p_yes = pm.Deterministic("p_yes", pt.clip(in_concept[row_cell], 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6))',
'''    # Report stage: each person's criterion shifts the belief log-odds.
    belief = pt.clip(in_concept[row_cell], 1e-9, 1 - 1e-9)
    logit_b = pt.log(belief) - pt.log1p(-belief)
    p_known = pm.math.sigmoid(logit_b + crit_sd * crit_z[row_person])

    person = np.clip(starts - 1, 0, MAX_PEOPLE - 1)
    known = known & (starts > 0)
''',1)
